scope: A1 external image exception rollback and concurrent filename ownership for Markdown export; not crash-safe multi-file atomicity
implementation: ExitStack tracks only newly created assets; a private context extends through Document main-file encoding and atomic publication. Exclusive O_CREAT|O_EXCL pending markers prevent other writers from claiming or reusing rollback-eligible images; own repeated bytes reuse the owned image. Markers always clean up on ordinary exit; new images clean up on failure only.
coverage: Real python-docx picture plus Chinese paragraph plus merged table
ASCII and unknown codec failures; strict late merge-loss diagnostic; main output replace error; later image write error
Existing unrelated and equal-content reused files survive; original Markdown remains; direct writer can be reused after failure
Interleaved successful same-content export survives another export ASCII rollback
Two simultaneous exports compete for the first marker through a thread barrier; links resolve to independently checked red and blue image pixels after both exports finish
Pending claim descriptor-close error removes the newly created marker

installed_integration.selection: markdown or md_writer or image_collision or conversion_api or bounded_conversion or ecosystem_semantics or field_shape_visibility or nested_field_visibility
installed_integration.boundary: Installed wheel from /tmp with --import-mode=importlib; targeted integration, not a fresh full suite

common_markdown.result: Five fixed inputs retain identical bytes, hashes and diagnostics

limits: Ordinary exception rollback is not power-loss or process-kill safe multi-file publication
An interrupted process can leave assets or pending markers; occupied names are skipped, not automatically deleted
New empty directories may remain after rollback
Controlled thread interleaving is validated on this local filesystem; independent-process and network-filesystem concurrency not accepted
No new native Word/LibreOffice or PDF layout acceptance; remaining A1/A4 gaps stay open
